manifest.title: Elite War Wagon: tape versus simulation diagnosis
manifest.description: All six standard-unit outcomes and a full-rate diagnosis of the Paladin reversal.

blocks.body: # Elite War Wagon: tape versus simulation diagnosis

## Paladin is a singular engagement failure, not a generally overpowered War Wagon

Four of the six standard-unit rows are winner-correct with absolute deltas between **1.60 and 12.51 points**. The Battle Elephant row never terminates. Paladin is the sole resolved reversal: tape has Paladin winning all four repeats with **30.00–39.80%** remaining HP, while all five simulations give War Wagon the win with **83.33%** remaining HP. The **118.77-point delta** is caused primarily by Paladins converging on one target, losing movement under crowd pressure, and never penetrating the Wagon collision envelope. Tape records some Wagon–Paladin overlap in **26.0–43.7% of frames**; simulation records none. War Wagon base speed, normalized firing rate, Paladin first-hit timing, and Paladin damage after attack start are close to tape.

## Five resolved controls isolate Paladin as the outlier

Champion is almost exact and falls inside the observed tape band. Arbalester, Heavy Cavalry Archer, and Heavy Scorpion retain the correct winner with single-digit to low-teens deltas. That pattern argues against changing War Wagon HP, raw damage, range, or general kiting policy before fixing the Paladin engagement bottleneck.

## The fight begins correctly and then diverges at sustained contact

Paladins land their first damage at **3.45s** in simulation versus **3.58–3.60s** on tape, so the opening attack-move and initial arrival are not late. After that, tape Paladins deal all **3,000 War Wagon HP**, while simulation Paladins deal only **500 HP** and kill one Wagon. Tape records **219–223 Paladin attack starts**; simulation records only **35**. Yet hit completion after an attack begins is **97.1%** in simulation versus **93.7–95.9%** on tape. Damage arithmetic is functioning—the Paladins are not being allowed to start enough attacks.

## Target concentration creates the crowd jam

Tape Paladins pursue a median of **5–6 distinct War Wagons**, with the largest target group holding **38.5–45.5%** of current targets. Simulation collapses to **one distinct target and 100% concentration**. The direct paths therefore converge through the same allied cluster. Actual Paladin speed while position changes falls from **1.485 tiles/s** on tape to **0.955**, and stalled chase observations rise from **12.7–13.6%** to **34.9%**.

## Tape forms a surrounding contact front; simulation forms a queue

In tape, **6–11 Paladins** can simultaneously sit within 0.25 surface tiles of a Wagon and **7–10** can attack at once. Simulation reaches only **one** Paladin in that close shell and at most **two** simultaneous attackers. The robust P10 surface gap is **0.10–0.15 tiles** on tape versus **0.57** in simulation. Rare tape frames go deeper, but matching the extreme overlap is unnecessary; the important target is sustained multi-unit access around several Wagons.

## War Wagons overlap heavily in tape—and even more persistently in simulation

Using the 0.45-tile Wagon radius, tape has at least one Wagon–Wagon overlap in **80.9–93.4% of combat frames**, and **66.9–80.4%** of live-Wagon observations overlap at least one Wagon ally. Conditional median overlap depth is **0.299–0.325 tiles**. Simulation is denser: **99.2%** of frames have overlap, **97.9%** of live-Wagon observations overlap an ally, and the median depth is **0.420 tiles**. Extreme tape frames reach nearly coincident centers, but the sustained medians—not those extremes—show that same-team Wagon stacking is genuine.

## Tape permits limited enemy penetration; simulation permits none

A Wagon and Paladin overlap when their center distance falls below **0.70 tiles**. Every tape repeat contains this contact: overlap appears in **26.0–43.7% of frames**, with a conditional median depth of **0.066–0.113 tiles** and P90 depth of **0.179–0.357**. At peak, **6–8 Wagon–Paladin pairs** overlap simultaneously; one Wagon overlaps up to **2–3 Paladins**, while one Paladin can overlap **4–6 Wagons** inside the already compressed Wagon blob. Simulation records **zero** cross-team overlaps; its closest pair still has a **+0.055-tile surface gap**. This hard separation is a second confirmed reason Paladins cannot build a multi-unit attack front.

## War Wagon mechanics are not the primary lever

Observed Wagon movement speed is **1.300–1.306 tiles/s** on tape and **1.320** in simulation. Normalized firing is **34.5–36.3 attack starts per 100 alive-Wagon seconds** on tape versus **37.2** in simulation—a modest overshoot, not enough to explain the winner reversal. Raw simulation attack totals are larger because almost every Wagon survives for the entire fight. The kiting clock should remain unchanged for the first experiment.

## Recommended engine experiment: distribute melee targets and permit bounded contact capture

Do not add a War-Wagon-versus-Paladin exception and do not shrink either collision box. First, add a general congestion cost based on allied pursuers already assigned to a target and occupied approach sectors around it. A chaser whose direct path crosses a saturated allied group should select another reachable enemy or persist around the tangent to an unoccupied sector. Second, allow bounded swept contact capture when a melee chaser reaches a valid moving-target envelope; tape supports modest cross-team penetration but not unrestricted pass-through. Preserve the allied-overlap cap. Together these changes should prevent the one-target queue and let several Paladins form the contact front visible in tape.

## Method and definitions

The four authorized `frames.bin` members were decoded at full render cadence and filtered to live masters 829 and 569. HP changes, action-state transitions, targets, paths, collision-surface gaps, and simultaneous contact counts were measured from first active movement/targeting through the final death. The simulation used the exact canonical 15v17 starting roster, coordinates, golden map, sample 0, and seed 20260817. All five saved simulation samples have the same final score. Surface gap is Euclidean center distance minus the fixture radii: 0.90 tiles combined for Wagon–Wagon and 0.70 for Wagon–Paladin. A negative gap is overlap; overlap depth is its absolute value. Pair share uses every live pair observation, while unit share asks whether each live unit overlaps at least one comparison unit in that frame.

## Limitations and robustness

Tape action-state 7 is a proxy for attack starts rather than a byte-identical engine event. HP drops can aggregate simultaneous projectile hits in one rendered frame, so ranged hit-event counts are less directly comparable than melee attack-start and damage-completion rates. Overlap is measured from sampled centers and circularized collision extents; it establishes positional penetration but not the game's private collision decision. Exact near-coincident centers are therefore treated as outliers, while the frame, unit, median, and P90 measures carry the conclusion. The diagnosis is supported by four consistent tape repeats and one deterministic trace whose final result matches all five saved samples, but the proposed mechanics still require a controlled experiment and regressions.

## Next step and decision gate

Implement the general target-distribution plus bounded-contact experiment, run only the 15v17 War Wagon–Paladin row first, and compare five samples with these trace targets: **5–6 distinct Paladin targets, 26.0–43.7% of frames with some Wagon–Paladin overlap, 6–8 simultaneous overlap pairs, 7–10 simultaneous attackers, 12.7–13.6% stalled chase, and 219–223 attack starts**. If those mechanics move toward tape and Paladin becomes the winner, then run the other five War Wagon controls to ensure Champion, Arbalester, HCA, and Scorpion do not regress and the Elephant timeout does not worsen.

## What would falsify this diagnosis?

If spreading Paladin targets and preserving tangent detours restores contact metrics but Paladin damage remains near 500 HP, the next suspect would be the melee engagement envelope around a large moving target. If contact and attack-start counts reach tape while the result still favors War Wagon, only then should War Wagon projectile resolution or recovery timing be investigated.

query.sql: SELECT matchup, ratio, tapeOutcome, tapeMean, tapeRange, simulationOutcome, simulationMean, simulationRange, absoluteDelta, status FROM war_wagon_matchups ORDER BY absoluteDelta DESC;
query.description: Selects all six exact golden Elite War Wagon rows from the completed recoverable benchmark.
filters: Exact golden starting roster, ratios, and positions
Five current-engine simulation attempts per stable row

metric_definitions.signed_outcome_score: Winner remaining HP divided by that winner's starting HP, multiplied by 100; positive means owner 3 and negative means owner 2.
metric_definitions.absolute_delta: Absolute difference between the simulation mean signed outcome and tape mean signed outcome.

query.sql: SELECT metric, tapeBand, simulation, unit, interpretation FROM diagnostic_metrics; SELECT metric, percentOfTapeMedian, tapeMedian, simulation, direction FROM contact_ratios ORDER BY percentOfTapeMedian ASC; SELECT * FROM wagon_wagon_overlap; SELECT * FROM wagon_paladin_overlap;
query.description: Compares four decoded full-rate frames.bin repeats with one exact-start current-engine trace; all five saved engine samples have the same final score.
filters: Combat window from first active movement/targeting through final death

metric_definitions.attack_start: Tape: transition into decoded action_state 7. Simulation: transition into the attacking action.
metric_definitions.effective_speed_while_moving: Observed path length divided by seconds in which the unit position changed; this captures collision and steering effects rather than nominal stat speed.
metric_definitions.surface_gap: Center-to-center distance minus the War Wagon and Paladin collision radii (0.45 and 0.25 tiles).
metric_definitions.overlap_depth: Negative surface gap expressed as a positive depth. Wagon-Wagon contact begins below 0.90 center tiles; Wagon-Paladin contact begins below 0.70 center tiles.
metric_definitions.overlap_pair_share: Overlapping pair observations divided by every live pair observation within the combat window.
metric_definitions.unit_overlap_share: Live unit observations in which that unit overlaps at least one unit from the named comparison population.
metric_definitions.stalled_chase_share: Chase-state observations where the unit's position did not change, divided by all chase-state observations.
metric_definitions.pursuit_target_concentration: Live Paladins grouped by their current target; the largest group divided by Paladins holding a target.
